THE DISCARDED EXTRAPOLATION FINISHED, AND ITS PREDICTION IS FALSIFIED BY YOUR RUNNING GATE. Recording this because it is direct evidence for the method point, and a trap worth avoiding when you pin the ceiling yourselves.

The invalid slice-shrinking measurement produced:

  slices=1  nodes=2184  analysis= 14.9s  us/node= 6826.5   (mean k 12.6)
  slices=2  nodes=4368  analysis= 53.1s  us/node=12156.1   (mean k 21.3)
  slices=3  nodes=6552  analysis=119.0s  us/node=18162.2   (mean k 24.9)

  naive mean seconds/node 0.01238
  naive projected ceiling 145377 nodes
  naive projection for the full 52416-node fixture: 10.8 MINUTES

Your gate has now run 47 min 55 s on that same fixture and has not finished. So the naive method underpredicted by at least 4.4x and would have reported a comfortable pass where the truth is a decisive fail.

The cause is visible in the table: per-node cost is not constant, it climbs 6826 -> 12156 -> 18162 microseconds as mean k grows 12.6 -> 21.3 -> 24.9. Shrinking slices shrinks the searchlights, and the k-by-k solve dominates. A second contaminant: these timings were taken while your gate worker was saturating a core, so they also measure contention.

Two of the three points would be needed to fit a k exponent, and they do not even agree - 1.10 between the first pair, 2.57 between the second - which is what you get when two uncontrolled variables move at once. Not salvageable; discarded in full.

WHAT STANDS. The bound taken directly from your gate, which needs no model:

  52416 nodes at mean k = 31.2 exceeds 30 minutes
  -> at fixed k and near-linear scaling in nodes, the 30-minute ceiling is at most
     52416 * 30/48 = 32760 nodes, and lower still since the run has not finished

So: dense-metric ceiling below roughly 33000 nodes at support size ~31. That is the number Epic 8 can state today, and it is now bounded by two independent observations rather than one.

WHEN YOU PIN IT PROPERLY: hold active_slices at 24 so k stays near 31, vary the IN-PLANE extent to change node count, run on a quiet machine, and report mean k alongside every timing so the normalisation is auditable.
